originalTitle: News live: Labor has ‘grave concerns’ for missing Australians in Nepal-Tibet flooding; Canavan claims ‘feminisation of curriculum’ led to rise of ‘manosphere’
content: Australian government bond yields hit 15-year high Australia’s 10-year interest rates have climbed to 5.23% and the highest in over 15 years as global bond markets are roiled by fears of stubbornly high inflation, the war on Iran, and ballooning government debts and deficits, especially in the United States. Higher borrowing costs threaten to put further pressure on federal and state budgets, where interest costs are already among the fastest rising expenses. Oil prices are pushing higher again after Iran reportedly attacked tankers attempting to pass through the gulf of Hormuz, triggering a fresh wave of American strikes that shattered weeks of relative calm. The international Brent crude benchmark passed $US95 a barrel on its way to its highest since 24 July, threatening to once again drive petrol prices higher over coming days and weeks. Kristalina Georgieva, the IMF’s managing director, in a statement marking the end of the G20 finance ministers’ meeting in the US said the world economy had navigated this year’s disruptions relatively well. But she rattled off a laundry list of worries: First, the energy shock is not over. Second, public debt – at almost 100 percent of GDP worldwide – now exceeds its post-World War II highs and is set to climb further. Third, the disinflation process has stalled in many countries. Mounting fiscal pressures are pushing core bond yields upward and the interplay between fiscal and monetary policy worries markets. Last, but not least, the future impact of AI on productivity and financial stability is dogged by unknowns.” Anthony Albanese has met with Palau’s president Surangel Whipps Jr at the Pacific Islands Forum this morning. On Wednesday, the government and Qantas confirmed more flights would travel between Brisbane and Koror, as part of the Palau Paradise Express direct air service. Qantas will also increase flights to twice weekly during Palau’s peak season, starting this December. A Queensland man has been charged with hate crime offences after a joint investigation by Queensland police and the Australian Federal Police. Official said they began an investigation into allegations of ideologically motivated threats of violence. On 27 August, they arrested a man, 52, in the Queensland town of Mossman and seized an electronic device. The man has since been charged with two counts of threats with circumstance of aggravation, including serious vilification or hate crime. Police will allege the offences relate to abusive, threatening and antisemitic content directed towards a religious organisation. The man is due to appear in court later this month. AFP detective supt Anthony Conway said in a statement: Harm to social cohesion at a local community level ultimately impacts on Australia’s national security – we will not allow divisive and hateful rhetoric to grow and spread more widely. Investigations are ongoing. Sydney’s ferry services hit by protected industrial action today from 9am to 2pm Members of the Maritime Union of Australia employed by Sydney Ferries are engaging in a five-hour work stoppage, with no ferries operating during that period. Services after the stoppage are expected to be significantly affected, and customers should continue to plan ahead and allow extra travel time. Members of the union will also undertake a ban on selling, collecting or validating tickets and fares from 1pm today until 2am Thursday. MUA members are seeking a 5% wage increase and guaranteed annual increases in subsequent years. MUA deputy branch secretary Paul Garrett said: Our members kept Sydney Ferries running throughout Covid, dealt with a fleet of 13 overseas-built and defect ridden vessels that were not fit for purpose, and have continued to work long and demanding hours to keep the public moving. They have always demonstrated their commitment to the job and to the travelling public, and they are now asking for a fair wage increase to catch up with the spiralling cost of living in this city. House prices could fall 10%, analysts predict, as fourth interest rate hike looms The prospect of the steepest property market downturn in history will not stop the Reserve Bank from delivering a fourth interest rate hike as it battles to bring inflation back under control, economists say. New data from Cotality revealed house prices are now falling in more than 90% of Australian suburbs, amid a perfect storm of higher borrowing costs, a weak economy, and a once-in-a-generation change in the tax treatment of property investors. Shane Oliver, AMP’s chief economist, said average home values would continue falling for the next six to nine months, by which time property prices nationally would be about 10% down from their recent peak. “That would be the worst in the postwar period,” Oliver said, although the figure is not hugely out of line with previous property market corrections in the order of 8% – most recently in 2022-23. Read more: ‘No one with a brain’ wants more affordable houses via taxation, Bragg says Liberal senator Andrew Bragg said no one wants to buy houses in Australia at the moment due to a system of high taxation, high regulation and a sinking economy. Bragg spoke to RN Breakfast this morning, lamenting the state of the economy without saying that falling house prices could make it easier for first home buyers to afford property. He said: If you want to get more affordability, the way you get there is more supply, not through more taxes, because more taxes actually destroys the ability of younger people to pay a reasonable level of rent. It reduces the number of houses people can live in, and so no one wants to see affordability pursued through more taxes. No one with a brain would do that. And so what we’re seeing now are the consequences of these terrible tax grabs. Bragg was asked multiple times if there was an ongoing correction in the housing market. chineseContent: 澳大利亚政府债券收益率创15年新高澳大利亚10年期利率已攀升至5.23%，为15年来的最高水平，原因是全球债券市场因对持续高通胀、伊朗战争以及政府债务和赤字膨胀（尤其是美国）的担忧而动荡。较高的借贷成本可能会给联邦和州预算带来进一步的压力，而利息成本已经是增长最快的支出之一。据报道，伊朗袭击了试图穿越霍尔木兹湾的油轮，引发美国新一波袭击，打破了数周的相对平静，油价再次走高。国际布伦特原油基准价格突破每桶 95 美元，升至 7 月 24 日以来的最高水平，有可能在未来几天和几周内再次推高汽油价格。国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃在美国二十国集团财长会议结束的声明中表示，世界经济相对较好地应对了今年的干扰。但她列出了一系列担忧：首先，能源冲击尚未结束。其次，公共债务 — — 几乎占全球 GDP 的 100% — — 现在已经超过了二战后的高点，并且还将进一步攀升。第三，许多国家的通缩进程陷入停滞。不断增加的财政压力正在推高核心债券收益率，财政和货币政策之间的相互作用令市场担忧。最后但并非最不重要的一点是，人工智能对生产力和金融稳定的未来影响仍存在未知数。”安东尼·阿尔巴内塞今天上午在太平洋岛屿论坛上会见了帕劳总统小苏兰吉尔·惠普斯。周三，政府和澳洲航空确认，布里斯班和科罗尔之间将有更多航班往返，因为
